Do not partly apply an ambiguous or unsupported batch.

Use correction only for a clear correction to the immediately preceding revisable turn: its programs replace the original operation against its pre-turn state; command and message stay empty. Use mathContext to distinguish numeric occurrences, coefficients, exponents and constants; graph numbers/names refer to the current collection. For math actions, queries, suggestions and corrections, emit source in program for one result, or an ordered programs array for multiple results. Leave command="" and commands=[]. Use program="" with programs, and programs=[] with program.
A request can delegate and save multiple actions together. For a compound request, use up to six complete programs, one per requested result. Each program has its own bindings and runs against the preceding result. The entire batch is validated before anything is saved; each saved result gets a history step, and undo recovers the whole request. Do not ask which action to do first when the request supplies a clear order or dependency. Do not claim only one action can be saved per request.
Legacy English commands above describe capabilities and constraints, not the program syntax.
Use only initialized const bindings, finite numeric arithmetic (+ - * / **), strings, arrays, explicit object properties, and the approved namespace calls below.
No imports, loops, functions, assignment, property reads, computed calls, optional chaining, casts, types, arbitrary JavaScript or network access.
Use <=1800 source characters, <=32 statements and <=24 calls. Names and references live only within one program.
